and its masters surrendered it in peace.
And he gave it to Nasir al-Din Manguras bar Kumartakin, the slave of Mujahid al-Din bar Buzan.
And he also took Shughr-Bakas.
And from there he went to Darbsak,
and he attacked it and took it.
And he went again against Baghras;
and there were not enough warriors in it,
and the chief of the Templars who was in it surrendered it.
And when all these places fell to the Arabs,
the people of Antioch were very afraid,
especially because the roads were blocked before them,
and grain was cut off.
Therefore the Prince humbled himself before Saladin,
and sent requesting peace.
And he made peace with him for a period of eight months,
and left and went to Aleppo.
And from there he went to Damascus,
and rested for a few days.
And he set out and went and encamped against Safed and attacked it fiercely,
and they surrendered it to him.
And he also took the fortress of Kawkab after great distress.
And in this same year died Muwaffaq As'ad, the physician of Damascus,
who was known as Ibn al-Mitran.
For this man,
because of the honor of the passing world,
abandoned his faith and converted to Islam.
And he acquired great wealth,
and Saladin betrothed him to one of his maidservants.
And after a short time he died,
and his name perished.
For even after the death of Saladin his wife was seen with a boy who was dear to him,
as they went round to the houses of the notables and begged for alms.

And Reynald, the lord of Sidon,
who, when it had been taken from him, went and dwelt in the cliff of Arnun (Beaufort),
having received a promise from Saladin,
came out to him and requested of him a condition for up to three months,
so that he might bring out his people from Tyre,
and then take a place that would be sufficient for him in the territory of Damascus,
and surrender that cliff.
Saladin permitted him.
Then Saladin perceived that Reynald was deceitfully flattering him in his craftiness,
and that he did not cease from digging the ditch and building the wall.
